page.title: 3D model to brick converter | MOCsmith
page.description: Turn a 3D model into a brick model you can really build: change the size, recolour it, build it step by step, compare it with the original. Everything runs in your browser.

start.title: Turn a 3D model into bricks you can build
start.lead: Pick a sample or bring your own model. Change the size, recolour it and build it step by step, all in this page.
start.file.title: I have a model file
start.file.note: A .glb 3D model (from any image-to-3D site), or an .ldr / .mpd brick model saved from Studio or LeoCAD.
start.image.title: I have a brick-style AI picture
start.image.note: Upload a picture: it becomes a 3D model, then bricks. Image-to-3D isn't connected yet, so uploading is off for now.
start.image.tips: One thing per picture, shown whole, on a clean background, without strong reflections or shadows.
start.prompt.what: Paste this into ChatGPT, Gemini or any AI image tool and replace the part in brackets with what you want to build. It asks for a picture that suits bricks: plain bricks only, sturdy, no overhangs, few colours, one object, no baseplate, matte, light grey background, seen from the front corner. You can turn the picture into a .glb file with an image-to-3D tool, then add it in the “I have a model file” card.
start.prompt.copied: Prompt copied. Paste it into your AI tool.
start.prompt.manual: The browser did not allow copying. The full text is selected: press Ctrl+C (⌘C on a Mac).

start.mosaic.title: Turn a photo into a flat mosaic
start.mosaic.note: Like a LEGO® Art picture: 1×1 round or square tiles, with the base plates and a parts list. The photo is processed in your browser and never uploaded.
start.mosaic.examples: Or try one of these first

mosaic.title: {name} · flat mosaic
mosaic.frame.caption: Whole photo (the framed part becomes the mosaic)
mosaic.frame.note: Drag inside the frame to move it, drag a corner to resize, drag outside to draw a new one; the frame's shape sets the grid. Keyboard: arrow keys move, Shift + arrows resize, Esc finishes.
mosaic.frame.aria: Framed part of the photo: left {x}%, top {y}%, width {w}%, height {h}%
mosaic.canvas.aria: The photo as a brick mosaic, {w} × {h} studs
mosaic.size.frame: To use only part of the photo, press “Frame a part” under the photo.
mosaic.colours.locked: While only your sets are used, the colour limit and dithering are fixed: both change how many of each colour are used.
mosaic.relief.size: The first time it downloads a depth model of about 30 MB.
mosaic.dither.note: Dithering smooths gradients, but on photos it scatters specks of other colours. Floyd–Steinberg gives smoother gradients, Atkinson sharper ones; the default is none.
mosaic.private: The photo is processed on this page only and sent nowhere.
mosaic.base.notFit: Width and height must both be multiples of {side}
mosaic.base.fitHint: The picture is {w} × {h} studs now, so the greyed-out baseplates can't be used. Use “Frame a part” to change its shape, or pick another size, so both sides are multiples of 48 (or 32).
mosaic.base.panelsNote: {count} 16 × 16 panels joined by {pins} Technic pins into one piece, as in LEGO Art.
mosaic.base.oneNote: One baseplate holds the whole picture.
mosaic.base.manyNote: {count} baseplates side by side. Baseplates do not clip together: glue or screw them to a board, or put them in a frame.
mosaic.pdf.cover: One {part} per cell, by the colour numbers on each base’s page.
mosaic.pdf.baseNote: The number in each cell is its colour (see the key); a white line every 4 cells helps you keep your place.
mosaic.pdf.failed: The PDF could not be made ({why}).
mosaic.pdf.raiseNote: This picture stands out in places: lay the layer 1 plates on the base as drawn, then the layer 2 plates on top of them (the pale area is the layer underneath), then turn the page and lay the surface parts by number. All plates are black.
mosaic.pdf.raiseNoteOne: This picture stands out in places: lay the plates on the base as shown, then turn the page and lay the surface parts by number. The plates are black.
mosaic.pdf.raiseCover: Relief (2.5D): {n} black plates raise the near parts; each base has a raise-plate page before its own.
mosaic.download.note: The parts list imports into Rebrickable. The .ldr opens in Studio or LeoCAD: the base first, then one step per 16 × 16 block.
mosaic.own.note: Tick the LEGO Art sets you have, or search for any other set (add one more than once if you have several): no colour is used more often than those boxes hold, and what is missing is listed to buy.
mosaic.own.enough: The boxes hold {have} of these parts and this picture uses {n}: enough of them. The colour cap and dithering are off while sets are in use, since both change how many of each colour are used.
mosaic.own.short: The boxes hold {have} of these parts and this picture needs {n}: {used} come from the boxes and {buy} are to buy (marked in the colour list). The colour cap and dithering are off while sets are in use, since both change how many of each colour are used.
mosaic.stockMode: When a box colour doesn't fit
mosaic.own.noSets: No LEGO Art set comes with this part.
mosaic.own.nonePart: {n} sets added, none with these parts: any colour
mosaic.own.nonePart#one: {n} set added, none with these parts: any colour
mosaic.own.badFit: These boxes' colours are far from this photo's (mean colour difference {e}, {free} with any colour), so the picture will not look much like the photo.
mosaic.relief.on: Raise what is near in the photo
mosaic.relief.note: Black plates go under the near cells, so the picture has height. The first use downloads a depth model of about 30 MB (Depth Anything V2) from Hugging Face; the photo is still processed on this page only.
mosaic.relief.mark: Mark the raised cells on the picture (lighter = higher)
mosaic.relief.downloading: Downloading the depth model: {loaded} of {total} MB
mosaic.relief.working: Working out what is near and what is far…
mosaic.relief.failed: Could not work out near and far ({why}); the mosaic works as before.

result.view.aria: 3D view of the brick model. Drag to turn, scroll or pinch to zoom
result.step.sub: Sub-assembly {i} of {total}: build it upside down on the table, then attach it from below in one piece
result.step.attach: First attach the finished {list} from below
result.step.fromBelowToo: This step's parts also go on from below
result.step.needsShow: Show these on the model; tap again to show the whole step
result.step.fromBelow: From below: turn the model over and press these on
result.allJoined.long: Every part is joined: nothing falls off when you lift it.
result.hist.title: Edit history
result.hist.note: Click a step to bring the model back to just after it; the later steps stay, so you can click them again or use Redo.
result.paint.title: Colour to paint with
result.paint.hint: Pick a colour, then tap parts on the model one at a time. A part LEGO never made in that colour stays as it is, and the line below says so.
result.paint.notMade: LEGO never made this {kind} in {colour}, so it stays as it is.
result.move.toolHint: Tap a part on the model to pick it up, then tap where it goes; Esc puts it back.
result.delete.hint: Tap parts on the model to remove them one at a time; a part with others on top can't be removed. Undo brings one back.
result.select.hint: Tap a part on the model to move it, turn it, change its colour or remove it.
result.gesture: Drag to turn · pinch or scroll to zoom
result.recolour.hint: Tap a colour to change all of it, or tap one piece on the model to change just that one.
result.info.aria: Part number and details of this piece
book.title: Building instructions
book.pdfFailed: The PDF could not be made ({why}). Use the browser’s Print to save it as a PDF.
book.cover.chapters: In {n} chapters; {subs} sub-assemblies are built on the table first
book.cover.made: LEGO has made every part in its colour.
book.cover.connected: All parts hold together: it will not fall apart when you pick it up.
book.cover.detached: {n} parts are not connected and will fall off when you pick it up; take care with them.
book.cover.detached#one: {n} part is not connected and will fall off when you pick it up; take care with it.
result.takeaway.note: Open the model file in Studio or LeoCAD to keep editing; it has the same steps as build mode. Import the parts list into Rebrickable to find the parts.
result.tune.slow: Models longer than 32 studs take a fraction of a second; the result appears when you let go.
result.tune.repair: Rejoin parts that are not connected
result.tune.parts.always: Bricks and plates are always used; you can leave out the ones below.
result.tune.hangingHelp: Usually held from above, so not always a problem.
result.tune.part.round: Round parts (lone 1×1 and 2×2 posts and dots)
result.tune.delight: Remove light and shadow painted into the texture
result.tune.delightNote: For models made from photos: the shaded side of one colour no longer turns a shade darker. Parts designed in two shades (a dark roof on light walls) may be evened out too, so it starts off.
result.tune.thicken: Thicken 1-stud posts and legs to 2 studs
result.tune.thickenNote: Then they can use 2×2 parts instead of a stack of 1×1s, which holds better. It changes the shape (grows into the model, never fills gaps), so it starts off. Walls one stud thick already hold, so they stay.
result.tune.coloursNote: For when too many colours make the parts hard to collect: rarely used colours close to another go first, and small spots such as eyes stay. The samples' colours are designed, so it starts with no limit.
result.own.note: Add the sets you have (the same set more than once if you have several), or import parts lists exported from Rebrickable. The model then uses only those colours and your parts first; whatever is short goes on a to-buy list.
result.own.csv: Import parts lists (.csv, several at once)
result.own.read: {used} usable pieces, {skipped} skipped (parts or colours this page doesn't use)
result.own.badHeader: {name}: the first row needs Part, Color and Quantity columns (Rebrickable's parts-list format).
result.own.use: Uses {have} of your pieces; {buy} more to buy.
result.own.recoloured: Colours you don't have became the nearest you do: {list}.
result.own.setLineSkipped: {year} · {used} of {total} pieces usable ({skipped} this page can't use)
